title: नयनराज पाण्डेको जियारामाथि नारीवादी चिन्तनः एक अध्ययन {Feminist Reflections on Nayanraj Pandey's Ziara: A Study}
authors: न्यौपाने Nyaupane, दीपा पोख्रेल Deepa Pokhrel
nepali: नयनराज पाण्डेको कथा जियाराले मधेसका महिला हिंसाको पर्दाफास गरेको छ । यसले पितृसत्तात्मक प्रणालीबाट पीडित मधेसी महिलाहरूको दुर्दशाको उजागर गर्नु का साथै कपटी विरुद्ध साहसपूर्वक लड्ने महिलाहरूलाई पनि चित्रण गर्दछ तसर्थ यो अध्ययनले पितृसत्तात्मक समाजमा मधेसी महिलाले भोग्नुपरेका समस्याहरूको खोजी गर्दै “जियारा” कथामा विशेष ध्यानकेन्द्रित गरेको छ । यसले मधेसी समुदायमा महिलामाथि हुने उत्पीडन, दुर्व्यवहार र हिंसाका कारणहरूलाई चित्रण गर्छ । प्रस्तुत लेखले पितृसत्ता विरुद्ध प्रतिक्रिया दिन मधेसी महिलाहरूले प्रयोग गर्ने  तरिकाहरूको विश्लेषण गर्दछ । यी उद्देश्यहरूलाई सम्बोधन गर्न, नारीवादी सिद्धान्त, मुख्यतया केट मिलेटले परिकल्पना गरेको कट्टरपन्थी नारीवादीको आलोचनात्मक अन्तर्दृष्टिलाई परीक्षण अन्तर्गत उक्त कथाको विश्लेषण गर्न सैद्धान्तिक मापदण्डहरूको रूपमा प्रयोग गरिएको छ । पितृसत्तात्मक समाजले महिलामाथि दमन गर्न पनि पुरुषलाई स्वीकृति दिन्छ । केट मिलेटको सिद्धान्त अनु सार पुरुषहरूले पितृसत्ता सिर्जना गर्छन् र यसलाई कायम राख्छन् किनभने तिनीहरूसँग स्रोतहरू छन् । त्यस्तै, पितृसत्ताले महिलालाई दास बनाउन मद्दत गर्छ । तसर्थ, यौन शोषण र उत्पीडनको विरुद्ध लड्न महिलाहरूबाट पितृसत्तात्मक समाजले उनीहरूका लागि तोकेको अधीनस्थ स्थितिलाई अस्वीकार गर्न आवश्यक छ । यस अध्ययनको सान्दर्भिकता पाठकलाई जियारा सङ्ग्रह हेर्नको लागि फरक दृष्टिकोणमा योगदान दिनु हो किनभने यस कथानकमा पाण्डेले पुरुषको वर्चस्वलाई समर्थन गर्ने सामाजिक–सांस्कृतिक अभ्यासका कारण मधेसी महिलाले भोग्नुपरेको समस्यालाई प्रकाश पारेका छन् । ‘जियारा’ मा मुख्य महिला पात्रहरू पितृसत्तात्मक सामाजिक व्यवस्थाको सिकार भएका छन् ।
american_english: Nayanraj Pandey's story Ziara exposes the violence against Madhesi women. Along with revealing the plight of Madhesi women suffering under the patriarchal system, it also depicts women who fight courageously against hypocrites. Therefore, this study, while investigating the problems Madhesi women have had to endure in patriarchal society, has focused special attention on the story "Ziara." It portrays the causes of the oppression, abuse, and violence that occur against women in the Madhesi community. The present article analyzes the methods Madhesi women employ to resist patriarchy. To address these objectives, feminist theory — primarily the critical insight of radical feminism as conceptualized by Kate Millett — has been used as theoretical criteria to analyze the aforementioned story. Patriarchal society also permits men to oppress women. According to Kate Millett's theory, men create and maintain patriarchy because they control resources. Similarly, patriarchy helps make women into slaves. Therefore, in order to fight against sexual exploitation and harassment, it is necessary for women to reject the subordinate position assigned to them by patriarchal society. The contextual relevance of this study is to contribute a different perspective for viewing the text Ziara because in this narrative Pandey has highlighted the problems Madhesi women have had to endure due to socio-cultural practices that support male dominance. The main female characters in "Ziara" are victims of the patriarchal social system.

informal_english: Nayanraj Pandey's story Ziara pulls back the curtain on violence against Madhesi women. It doesn't just show how rough Madhesi women have it under the patriarchy — it also gives us women who straight-up fight back against the hypocrites. So this study digs into the problems Madhesi women deal with in a patriarchal society, zeroing in on "Ziara." It breaks down why oppression, abuse, and violence happen to women in the Madhesi community. The article looks at how Madhesi women push back against the patriarchy. To get at this, it uses feminist theory — mainly Kate Millett's take on radical feminism — as the lens for analyzing the story. The patriarchy lets men oppress women, plain and simple. Millett says men build and keep the patriarchy going 'cause they hold all the cards, resource-wise. It also turns women into second-class citizens. Bottom line: if women want to fight sexual exploitation and harassment, they've gotta reject the subordinate role the patriarchy hands them. This study matters 'cause it gives a fresh angle on Ziara — Pandey uses the story to call out the socio-cultural BS that props up male dominance and makes life hell for Madhesi women. The main female characters in "Ziara"? They're victims of the system, pure and simple.
